key_insight: An additive thermodynamic correction layer aligns machine learning interatomic potentials with assessed phase stability without retraining the base model.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables more accurate melting and solid-state transformation temperatures while retaining transferable atomistic models.
method: Convert required phase free-energy shifts into configuration energy targets using a first-order thermodynamic construction.
Fit an additive linear atomic cluster expansion correction.
Refine the correction iteratively using measured free energies.
evidence_signal: With a foundation GRACE model, all tested transformation temperatures reached prescribed tolerances, including joint solid–solid and melting corrections for Ca, Ti, and Zr.
watch_item: Large corrections can change vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density, requiring validation beyond transition temperatures.
paper_title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
